full-stack / AfterBell

One platform, three different workflows

How the AfterBell frontend and backend support students, employers and administrators.

React / TypeScript → Flask API → Supabase Auth + Database → Role-specific workflows

The problem

Students need to discover opportunities and manage applications. Employers need to post roles and review applicants. Administrators need tools for verification and user management. AfterBell brings these related workflows into a single platform.

Frontend and backend

The repository contains a React / TypeScript frontend built with Vite and a Python Flask backend. Supabase provides authentication and database services. The frontend handles the user interface while the backend exposes the application API.

Role-specific workflows

Student features include job browsing, saved jobs and applications. Employer views support job posting and applicant management. Administrator views include user management and employer verification. These are repository-supported features, not a claim that every deployed workflow has been exercised.

AI-assisted extraction

The backend includes extraction of job information from images, using Groq with a Gemini fallback. This supports the job-information workflow; the portfolio does not describe it as an automated hiring or candidate-ranking system.

Scope of the evidence

The source structure and implementation were reviewed. A publicly hosted frontend is referenced in the README, but authenticated production workflows have not been verified, so the repository is the primary link here.
